newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-CHALLENGERS DRAW TO LEAVE INTER TOP OF SERIE A.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHALLENGERS DRAW TO LEAVE INTER TOP OF SERIE A.

text.p: Internazionale stayed top in Italy on Sunday when Vicenza wasted an historic chance to lead Serie A and European champions Juventus and AC Milan played out a scoreless draw.

Vicenza, who have never held the sole lead in Serie A, could have leapfrogged over Inter at the top with a win over lowly Verona after the Milan club were held to a 2-2 home draw by Fiorentina on Saturday.

But Francesco Guidolin's side were lucky to come away with a draw after an own goal by captain Giovanni Lopez and a goal by Filippo Maniero gave their northeast Veneto rivals an early 2-0 lead in a hard-fought derby.
Striker Roberto Murgita cut the gap in the 36th minute and Verona defender Marco Baroni returned Lopez's favour with an own goal 11 minutes from time.

Under rain in Turin, Juventus could have joined Inter at the top but they could have lost as well against a tough Milan side. Liberian striker George Weah came close midway through the first half and Marco Simone also threatened a goal for the visitors late in the game.
Michele Padovano had two chances for Juventus after the interval but hit the bar and then ran into veteran sweeper Franco Baresi, in fine form after several weeks' absence through injury.
Milan are now seventh, four points behind Inter and level on points with Roma, 3-1 home winners over former coach Carlo Mazzone's Cagliari, and Sampdoria, who drew 1-1 at home with Parma.
Roma's Argentine international Abel Balbo struck twice to become Serie A's top scorer with eight goals.
Juventus are two points back along with Bologna, whose Swedish and Russian internationals Kennet Andersson and Igor Kolyvanov both scored in a 3-1 comeback victory against bottom club Reggiana.
At Genoa, Italy striker Enrico Chiesa equalised with seven minutes left to give Parma a 1-1 draw over Sampdoria in his first match against his former club, who sold him last May.
"It's still 'work in progress'," Chiesa said of Parma, who are struggling with just 12 points from nine matches.

It was also Parma's first match without Gianfranco Zola, who made his debut for English side Chelsea on Saturday, while it could be Christian Karembeu's last game for Sampdoria. The Frenchman is tipped to move to Barcelona or Real Madrid.
Verona, Napoli and Udinese took to the pitch wearing black armbands in memory of their former goalkeeper Giuliano Giuliani, 38, who died of an AIDS-related illness this week.

Some 50,000 fans in Naples observed a minute's silence for him before their team's match against Perugia. Helped by two goals from Alfredo Aglietti, Napoli won 4-2 to move into fifth place in the table, a point behind European champions Juventus and Bologna..
Giuseppe Signori, whose missed penalty condemned Lazio to a 1-0 defeat at Napoli in a midweek Italian Cup tie, pulled off a hat-trick including a penalty to give the Rome side a 3-1 win at Piacenza.
At Bergamo, Atalanta exploited a 20th-minute own goal by defender Valerio Bertotto to surprise Udinese with a 1-0 win vital to the northern club's hopes of avoiding relegation.
